plugins.description: Run Claude Code over ACP on your AWS Bedrock account, set up from the plugin settings with your Bedrock API key. Forks and side chats work. In Accept Edits, Bash runs in Claude Code's sandbox, as with bb's own Claude Code provider, and /compact works. In plan mode the plan opens in the side panel and Claude waits for your go-ahead, even in Full Access. Estimated spend shows in the provider usage panel against a monthly budget. Requires Node.js and Amazon Bedrock access.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- **Claude Code (Bedrock ACP)** as a provider in the model picker. Threads run Claude Code through the ACP adapter and bill your AWS account instead of a Claude subscription. Forks and side chats work.
- Setup in the plugin settings: Bedrock API key, AWS region or profile. bb stores the key as a secret and the agent reads it from there; the plugin keeps no copy, and removing the plugin removes the key.
- **Estimated spend** in the Provider usage panel and footer: this month and today, against a monthly budget you set.
- A **price factor** for negotiated Bedrock pricing, for the cost bb shows in each thread and for the usage entry.
- Plan mode that waits for you: when Claude finishes a plan, it opens in the side panel of the thread you're looking at and follows later revisions, and you get Claude's "Ready to code?" question, even in Full Access, where bb would otherwise approve it on its own.
- A provider icon: the Claude mark with an AWS badge.

## How it works

The plugin registers its own provider, which bb runs through the plugin SDK's ACP bridge. The provider starts a launcher script that runs Claude Code in Bedrock mode over ACP with the bundled claude-agent-acp adapter, and a small proxy that records each thread's cost in a local ledger. Versions before 0.2 added a custom agent to bb's ACP agents plugin instead; the first load hands that over, and existing threads keep working.

The spend figures are Claude Code's own list-price estimates, not your AWS bill.

## Requirements

- bb 0.49 or later, on macOS or Linux (tested on macOS); the provider runs on the machine bb runs on
- Node.js and Claude Code (`claude` on PATH)
- Access to the Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock, with a Bedrock API key or AWS credentials

Details: https://github.com/alexkli/bb-plugin-acp-claude-bedrock#setup

plugins.description: Run Claude Code over ACP on your GitHub Copilot subscription, set up from the plugin settings with a GitHub sign-in. Copilot's GPT, Gemini and Grok models sit next to Claude in the model picker. Forks and side chats work. In Accept Edits, Bash runs in Claude Code's sandbox, as with bb's own Claude Code provider, and /compact works. In plan mode Claude waits for your go-ahead, even in Full Access. Each thread's Copilot credits show above the prompt, a usage page has the token dashboard, and your premium-request quota shows in the provider usage panel. Requires Node.js, Claude Code and a GitHub Copilot subscription.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- **Claude Code (Copilot ACP)** as a provider in the model picker. Threads run Claude Code through the ACP adapter on your GitHub Copilot subscription instead of an Anthropic login. Forks and side chats work.
- Every Copilot chat model in the model picker: Claude, plus GPT, Gemini, Grok and others through copilot-api's Messages translation.
- A settings page for GitHub sign-in with a device code, copilot-api start and stop, the default model, and the Copilot models behind Claude Code's opus, sonnet and haiku aliases.
- A **Copilot usage** page with copilot-api's token and cost dashboard. It also works from bb on a phone.
- The Copilot credits each thread has used, under the prompt next to the context-window control, with a breakdown by model. bb has no plugin slot there yet: if a bb update changes that row, the credits move to the composer's action row.
- Your Copilot premium-request quota in the Provider usage panel.
- Plan mode that waits for you: when Claude finishes a plan, it opens in the side panel of the thread you're looking at, and you get Claude's "Ready to code?" question, even in Full Access, where bb would otherwise approve it on its own.
- bb's permission modes: in Accept Edits, Bash runs in Claude Code's sandbox (writes stay in the workspace), as with bb's Claude Code provider; Full Access has none. `/compact` works too.
- `bb acp-claude-copilot` commands: status (checks the whole setup), repair, login, logout, start and stop. If the plugin can't register its provider, bb shows it as needing configuration, with the reason.

## How it works

The plugin ships a launcher script that runs Claude Code over ACP with the claude-agent-acp adapter (bundled, at a pinned version), and a small proxy in front of it. The proxy starts the plugin's own copilot-api (https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api) on a random local port with a generated key when a thread needs it, and points Claude Code at it. copilot-api stops after 30 idle minutes by default and starts again with the next message. The plugin registers its own provider, which bb runs through the plugin SDK's ACP bridge. Versions before 0.2 added a custom agent to bb's ACP agents plugin instead; the first load hands that over, and existing threads keep working.

It is independent of the Claude Copilot provider plugin, with its own sign-in and copilot-api; the two can be installed side by side.

## Requirements

- A GitHub Copilot subscription. Model availability and premium-request use follow your Copilot plan.
- bb 0.49 or later, on macOS or Linux (tested on macOS); the provider runs on the machine bb runs on
- Node.js and Claude Code (`claude` on PATH)

Details: https://github.com/alexkli/bb-plugin-acp-claude-copilot#setup

plugins.description: Run Claude Code threads on your AWS Bedrock account, with every feature bb's own Claude Code provider has. Threads use your Bedrock API key or AWS credentials instead of an Anthropic login, and the model picker lists the Bedrock models. Estimated spend shows in the provider usage panel against a monthly budget. Requires Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock access; the spend estimate needs Node.js.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- **Claude Code (Bedrock)**, a second Claude Code provider next to bb's own. Threads bill your AWS account through Amazon Bedrock instead of an Anthropic login.
- Everything bb's Claude Code provider does: plan mode, approvals and permission modes, subagents and workflows, skills, rewind and fork, compaction and the context meter.
- The Bedrock models Claude Code reports in the model picker, including inference profiles such as us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5.
- Estimated spend in the Provider usage panel and footer: this month and today, against a monthly budget you set, with a price factor for negotiated Bedrock pricing.
- Each thread's **session cost** in the context-window popup under the prompt.
- Setup in the plugin settings: Bedrock API key (stored as a bb secret), AWS region, AWS profile and an optional Claude Code executable.

## How it works

The plugin is bb's own Claude Code provider, copied unchanged at a bb release, under its own provider id. Bedrock is plain Claude Code configuration: the plugin gives this provider CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, the region and the credentials as environment, and a plain claude binary even when a machine-wide override points bb's Claude Code provider elsewhere.

The spend figures are Claude Code's own list-price estimates, recorded by a small wrapper around claude, not your AWS bill.

A weekly job in the plugin's repository picks up new bb releases of the provider, so fixes reach this plugin through updates.

## Requirements

- bb 0.49 or later
- Claude Code installed on the machine; Node.js for the spend estimate
- Access to the Anthropic models on Amazon Bedrock, with a Bedrock API key or AWS credentials. On macOS the plugin can also read the key from the keychain.

Details: https://github.com/alexkli/bb-plugin-claude-bedrock#setup

plugins.description: Run Claude Code threads on your GitHub Copilot subscription, with every feature bb's own Claude Code provider has. Copilot's GPT, Gemini and Grok models sit next to Claude in the model picker, and you sign in to GitHub from the plugin settings. A usage page shows the token dashboard, each thread's Copilot credits appear under the prompt, and your premium-request quota shows in the provider usage panel. Requires Claude Code and a GitHub Copilot subscription.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- **Claude Code (Copilot)**, a second Claude Code provider next to bb's own. It keeps bb's Claude Code features, such as plan mode, and runs on your GitHub Copilot subscription instead of an Anthropic login.
- Every Copilot chat model in the model picker: Claude, plus GPT, Gemini, Grok and others through copilot-api's Messages translation.
- A settings page for GitHub sign-in with a device code, copilot-api start and stop, the default model and reasoning level, and the Copilot models behind Claude Code's opus, sonnet and haiku aliases.
- A **Copilot usage** page with copilot-api's token and cost dashboard. It also works from bb on a phone.
- The Copilot credits each thread has used, under the prompt next to the context-window control, with a breakdown by model. bb has no plugin slot there yet: if a bb update changes that row, the credits move to the composer's action row.
- Your premium-request quota in the Provider usage panel.
- `bb claude-copilot` commands: status, login, logout, start and stop.

## How it works

The plugin runs its own copy of copilot-api (https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api) on a random local port with a generated key, and points only this provider's Claude Code at it. copilot-api stops after 30 idle minutes by default and starts again on the next turn.

## Requirements

- A GitHub Copilot subscription. Model availability and premium-request use follow your Copilot plan.
- Claude Code, with `claude` on PATH
- bb 0.49 or later

## Based on bb's Claude Code provider

The plugin contains a copy of bb's own Claude Code provider (MIT), so Copilot threads get the same features as normal Claude Code threads. It uses only public plugin API. A weekly job picks up changes to that provider from new bb releases.

plugins.description: A cozy pixel-art office where every thread is a little worker: busy threads at their desks, planners at the whiteboard, threads that need you in the waiting room, idle ones chatting over coffee and having lunch together. Thirteen places to put it, each with its own floor plan, pets and hidden easter eggs (classic, neon streets, redwood camp, surf villa, New York penthouse, dusty annex, school, startup house, mountain cabin, villain's lair, spaceship, coffee shop, and a home office where every thread works from its own little home and they meet on video calls), a short tour the first time you open it, your real weather outside, your providers' usage, an office TV, office events, festivals through the year and chiptune-style sound.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- A full-panel **pixel-art office** where every thread is a little worker. Where it is tells you what it's doing: busy threads at their desks, planners at the whiteboard, threads that need you in the waiting room, idle ones in the kitchen or lounge. One click puts a name tag over everyone, solid for unread and outlined for read.
- **Office life**: idle agents get together for coffee, a hallway chat, ping-pong or darts, with comic speech bubbles about tech news, small talk or what their thread did. They have lunch together after noon (pizza, sushi, burgers, tacos or ramen delivered, or a lunchbox). Someone occasionally gets a (harmless) shock in the server room, and a technician comes round to fix things, up a ladder if need be. At the mountain cabin they take the chairlift up and ski down together.
- **Plans for your review** are presented at the whiteboard in the glass meeting room. When you're writing a prompt for a thread, it sits in your office going over documents with you.
- **Thirteen sceneries**, one click away: the classic office, neon city streets, tents among the redwoods, a surf villa, a New York penthouse, a dusty forgotten annex, a school, a startup house, a mountain cabin, a villain's lair in a volcano, a spaceship, a coffee shop, and a home office where everyone works from home and meets on video calls. Each with its own floor plan, pets, visitors and things to click; same people and events, different world.
- **A short tour** the first time you open it, one thing at a time; take it again from the sticky-note legend.
- Desks furnished by **model** (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, GPT/Codex) with flat screens, the odd retro CRT and a Vision Pro or two, chairs by provider, and a shirt badge for what the thread is about.
- The office **remembers what you last saw**: coming back, only threads whose state changed get up and walk.
- A **home screen on the wall**: every enabled provider's usage on a pinboard, a calendar, a status light board, and a big TV with office news and live head counts, the office weather, tech headlines (Hacker News, Lobsters, Techmeme, The Verge, Ars Technica, DEV, Slashdot, the GitHub Blog, a mix, or any RSS or Atom feed) and, if you use the Work Dashboard plugin, your inbox.
- **Life in the office**: Biscuit the dog, Pixel the cat, a roomba, fish, a cleaning crew in the evening, a night guard, a glowing server room with an AI cluster, day and night with your clock, and your **real local weather** outside the windows.
- **Office events** for idle threads (parties, cake, karaoke, cornhole, darts, kids day…) and **festivals** through the year with decorations and their own party: snow day, Lunar New Year, Valentine's Day, Carnival, St. Patrick's Day, Holi, Easter, Maifest, summer, Oktoberfest, Halloween, Diwali, Laternenfest, Thanksgiving and the holidays.
- Lots to **click**, with synthesized sounds: the espresso machine, vending machine, piano, dartboard, plants, the globe, the couch, your own desk (whistles for the dog), and the windows (birds, crickets, rain, a foghorn…). Sound, scenery and the buddy live behind the gear at the top right. And every scenery hides a few easter eggs of its own for you to find.
- An **office buddy** that strolls in a corner of bb wherever you are (inside a thread, as that thread's figure), counting the threads with news since you last looked; the rail icon shows the same count.
- Fits any panel, even a phone held upright, and stays light: it pauses when off screen.

## Good to know

- Outside requests: the tech news source you picked for the TECH channel (at most every 20 minutes; `techNews false` turns it off), and the weather from Open-Meteo for your approximate location from your IP via geojs.io, or a place you set (`weather false` turns it off).
- Usage notes come from plugins that publish provider usage (most provider plugins do).
- Lunar New Year, Diwali and Holi dates are looked up through 2030.
- Furniture sprites from Pixel Agents (MIT).

plugins.description: Open any bb Settings page in one click from the sidebar footer. Pick built-in sections, plugin pages or project settings and put them in your order. It opens Settings pages through bb's URLs, so a bb update can break it until the plugin is updated.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- One icon per page in the sidebar footer. Click it and bb opens that Settings page.
- Providers and Projects by default. You can add any built-in Settings section, any enabled plugin's settings page or any project's settings.
- A settings page to choose and reorder the icons, with a filter over all pages.

## Good to know

- bb shows only a few plugin icons in the footer. The rest go into its More footer actions menu, in your order.
- Choices are stored per client, so the desktop app and a remote browser keep separate lists.
- After a change, the window reloads once, because bb registers footer items when the app loads.
- The plugin opens Settings URLs directly, since the plugin SDK has no route API. A bb update that changes Settings routes may need a plugin update.

plugins.description: See each thread's git branch and pull request status under its title in the sidebar. The pull request icon is colored by state, with a glyph for failing checks, running checks or ready to merge. Needs bb's thread row metadata experiment turned on.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

- The **branch** of the thread's environment, read live from bb's Git plugin. It is hidden on the default branch unless you turn that off.
- The **pull request** number, with an icon colored by state: open green, draft gray, merged purple, closed red.
- A status glyph on open pull requests: ✕ for failing checks, requested changes or conflicts, • for running checks, ✓ for ready to merge.
- Hover for the title, review state and check counts.

## Requirements

The metadata line under thread titles is a bb experiment. Turn it on with:

```sh
bb settings experiment threadRowMetadata true
bb thread-list prefs set showRowMetadata true
```

Pull request data comes from bb's GitHub PR Status plugin.

## Good to know

Where the plugin shows a pull request, it hides bb's own PR badge on that row. That relies on bb's sidebar markup, so a bb update could bring the duplicate back.
